law_name: Loi visant à sécuriser et réguler l'espace numérique (loi SREN)
description: As Minister Delegate for the Digital Transition, Barrot was the lead government sponsor of the SREN bill, transposing EU digital rules (DSA/DMA) and creating French measures on access to online pornography for minors, cyber-harassment, online scams and platform accountability. Definitively adopted 10 April 2024 and promulgated 21 May 2024.
significance: Major French law structuring online-space regulation; presented by Barrot as a tool to protect French citizens online.

law_name: Loi visant à encadrer l'influence commerciale (régulation des influenceurs)
description: Barrot, as Digital Minister, supported and helped shape the law regulating commercial influence on social media, which legally defines influencers, requires labelling of retouched/AI-altered images and bans the promotion of certain products (e.g. cryptocurrencies, cosmetic surgery).
significance: First French legal framework specifically regulating social-media influencers.

law_name: Dispositif anti-CumEx / CumCum (lutte contre l'arbitrage de dividendes)
description: As an MP and Vice-President of the Finance Committee, Barrot co-authored (with Bénédicte Peyrol) provisions adopted by the National Assembly in December 2018 to combat large-scale dividend-stripping tax-avoidance schemes (CumEx/CumCum), in the wake of the CumEx Files revelations.
significance: Strengthened French rules against dividend-arbitrage tax avoidance.

law_name: Proposition de loi rétablissant le vote par correspondance (vote par correspondance)
description: As an MP, Barrot (with Patrick Mignola) proposed a bill to (re)introduce postal voting to facilitate voting during the COVID-19 health crisis, ahead of the 2021 regional elections. The proposal was contested and not adopted.
significance: Notable but unsuccessful legislative proposal; illustrative of his parliamentary work, not enacted law.
